# Draft authored Memory grounding fixtures

These controlled source projects are not dd-tasks snapshots and are not
registered Eval cases. `minimal` exercises implemented code versus future
intent; `mature` exercises multiple source owners, current versus obsolete
descriptions, operational policy and genuine implementation limits. Both have
application code but no Memory Bank, unlike implemented dd-tasks checkpoints.

Only the selected `projects.json` source map is materialized into Subject input.
The separate draft expected-facts/preservation manifest stays Judge-side.
The offline test checks those bindings and exact blank Git materialization via
the existing Eval owner; passing it is not Subject/Judge semantic qualification.

Human acceptance must review the fact proposal, select a real immutable source
checkpoint and matching signed canon/CLI tuple, author all six stage contexts,
approve an assessment, and capture/qualify the entry pack. Operator-owned
Subject/Judge profiles and explicit execution authority are still required.
No accepted assessment, profile, entry pack or paid execution is created here.
